 Love Sargara Appellant(

 State Of Madhya Pradesh & Anr. Respondent
O R D E R Leave granted.

The appellant seeks suspension of sentence in connection with a case bearing Crime No. 518/22,
where the Trial Court convicted him for the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2)
(n), 376(2)(f), 376(3) and 342 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3 read with Section 4(2),
Section 5(l)(n) read with Section 6, Section 5(j)(ii) read with Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appeal filed by the appellant is pending consideration before the High Court.
Reason: CRL A @ SLP [CRL.] NO.14083/2025 was pleased to dismiss the second application for suspension of sentence filed by the appellant.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that there is a discrepancy with respect to the age of the victim, the witnesses have turned hostile and the appellant has been under incarceration for more than three years.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent- State submitted that there is no discrepancy with respect to the age and in the absence of any error, there is no need for interference.
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

Taking note of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant,
particularly, with respect to the discrepancies in the witness statements, the witnesses turning hostile, coupled with the period of incarceration already undergone, we are inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant during the pendency of his appeal.
Accordingly, the sentence of the appellant is suspended during the pendency of his appeal before the High Court and he is granted bail on terms and conditions to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
The appeal stands allowed, accordingly.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
